newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa sets up committee on gasoline prices.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa sets up committee on gasoline prices.

text.p: The South African Cabinet has appointed a special committee to review the pricing of gasoline, Cabinet Secretary Jakes Gerwel said on Friday.

In a statement, he said that the committee would review the government's future position on the marketing of petroleum activities return mechanisms (MPAR), as well as proposals on the possible future amendments to the oil price formula.
This followed a request from the oil industry for a three cents a litre wholesale margin increase.
The oil industry had hoped that its request for a wholesale margin increase, the first since September 1993, would be considered and approved at this week's Cabinet meeting.
But the usual statement by Gerwel at the end of the meeting made no mention of the application and government officials could cast no light on what had transpired.
The committee will consist of Mineral and Energy Affairs Minister Penuell Maduna, Transport Minister Mac Maharaj, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel and Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin.
Although Gerwel said that they had been asked to "urgently" consider the oil industry's case, he gave no indication of what timeframe was envisaged.

In terms of the MPAR, the oil industry has been due for a wholesale margin increase since January this year and it had hoped that it would be granted an increase in time for the next gasoline price adjustment due on November 6.

The Cabinet meets again on October 23 and the Central Energy Fund, which administers fuel price increases, has said that it would need to be advised of a margin increase by October 30 to include it in the next price adjustment.

The oil industry has warned that important investment decisions, including refinery expansions to meet growing demand, hung in the balance and that greater certainty about government's attitude to the oil industry, including pricing, was needed urgenty.
